explanation: An apostle who is the author of the letter to the Romans and a central figure in early Christianity.
A term for believers that shows close fellowship and love among members of the church.
An expression of friendship or gratitude sent to people Paul has met or heard about.
The community of Christian believers who gather to worship God, often called the church in Greek (ekklesia).
People dedicated to serving others and God's cause through work in the church.
The state in which a person is saved from the penalty of sin by faith in Jesus Christ.
God's undeserved favor given to people without merit, central to Christian teaching on salvation.
The real and true content of the gospel that Paul preaches against deception or falsehood.
The good news about God's kingdom through the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ.
